claims.harm: bitcoind coredumps with leveldb assertion failure when invalidateblock is called during index sync
claims.quote: If, at this commit, I am in the middle of syncing an index and at the same time call `invalidateblock` for the tip, my node coredumps
claims.settled_by_quote: Yes, I don't encounter this anymore now.

claims.harm: index sync blocks node operations and prevents graceful abort with SIGINT
claims.quote: Index Sync now seems to block everything else and makes it impossible to abort gracefully
claims.settled_by_quote: I tried to reproduce this again, but couldn't anymore. I must have made some error during my tests the last time.

claims.harm: race condition allows block connection notifications while ThreadSync is running during startup
claims.quote: Which would enable the index new block connection signals reception at the same time that `ThreadSync()` is being executed.

claims.harm: swallowing ReverseBlock() return value could hide errors if something is wrong with the index
claims.quote: Seems that we are swallowing `ReverseBlock()` return value. When it could mean that there is something wrong with the index.
claims.settled_by_quote: Good catch. It would be great if you want to follow up in different PR to reduce complexity here.

claims.harm: last cached header is incorrectly set to the disconnected block during rewind
claims.quote: This doesn't seem to be correct. The last cached header is being set to the block we just disconnected.
claims.settled_by_quote: This can be closed. I pushed it in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32694.
